cases.claim: All source and Game Forge project bytes match their digests.
The external game script parses without execution.
P1 and P2 movement, attacks, and dashes remain independently addressable.
Both players defend one reactor and receive one shared victory or defeat.
A standing nearby partner can revive a downed teammate; self-revive and distant revive are absent.
Each seat fires bounded visible bolts in its own facing direction.
Proximity is visibly disclosed and deterministically strengthens both seats without merging them.
Spark, runner, brute, and Warden behavior remains typed and bounded.
Eligible enemy defeats emit bounded green cores that visibly repair a damaged shared reactor.
The prebuild snapshot binds exact Asset Hands, Asset Fabric, and visual catalog declarations.
Every admitted known repair rule is applied before candidate source bytes are emitted.
The exact lobby, play, transition, outcome, and review-disclosure plan is byte-bound before candidate source.
Normal play keeps player-relevant information in the arena while technical truth remains available on demand.
Lobby, mission intro, active play, pause, outcome, and return-to-lobby states remain visibly coherent.
The live arena visibly uses the selected Neon Circuit palette, Aetherglass treatment constraints, portable FX, and distinct silhouettes.
Declared Asset Factory routes never become claims that asset artifacts were produced or installed.
Enemy, projectile, and repair-core state never exceeds declared ceilings.
The candidate uses no network, provider, persistence, filesystem, or dynamic-code surface.
Both keyboard seats visibly move their own avatar in the detached preview.
Visible start, pause, resume, and restart controls operate the same bounded engine.
The arena and control guide remain usable at desktop and narrow viewports.
Canvas summary, controls, focus visibility, and live status expose current play state.
Build and preview remain inside declared file, byte, entity, and process ceilings.
Reload and restart reset because persistence is explicitly unsupported.
